text: Hypothesis validated: terminal Product Proof semantics require verifier-owned canonical state mapping and terminal-safe action observation. Harbor Courier canary #3 exposed a real vocabulary mismatch: Director state_reached used failed/success, the proof planner recognized only success/failure, and the engine emits gameover/won. The prior planner could therefore omit a required failure-proof while still reporting reachability PASS. The active verifier could also erase a real won/gameover state by injecting another input that triggered the engine restart before polling observed the terminal. The validated repair canonically maps only the proven aliases won->success and failed/gameover->failure, preserves raw runtime states as evidence, fails closed on unsupported verifier states before Engineer spend, routes canonical terminal probes to independent success/failure scenarios, and stops periodic active input once a known terminal state is reached before performing the explicit harness-owned restart. Full branch and post-merge verifier regressions passed. This candidate remains inactive and is not promoted as an active Production lesson.
